messages:
sec_ops_bot: automated alert from supplychain-watchdog — suspicious publish detected for npm package 'supply-sdk'. versions 3.2.5 and 3.3.0 have a postinstall script that contacts `cdn.suspicious-exe[.]com`. flagged as high-confidence. vendor advisory link: https://supply-sdk.io/security/notice-2026-03-19
alex.kim: which services import supply-sdk? i'm oncall for payments and ingestion today.
samir: running dependency inventory now (`yarn why supply-sdk` + `npm ls supply-sdk` across monorepo). i'll post list shortly.
laura.platform: i'll block CI runners' egress to the npm registry and toggle pipelines to manual. also will create a temporary RBAC change to remove deploy rights from ci-runner until we confirm.
devsec_irma: recommend immediate steps: pin to last-known-good (3.2.4) OR rollback to last green builds, add package denylist, rotate any build-time tokens, and rewrap secrets in KMS.
sec_ops_bot: audit logs show two build jobs pulled 3.3.0 in the last 4h — projects: payments-integration (build id 9872), repo-batch-job (build id 9873). logs snippet:
```
build 9872: npm install supply-sdk@3.3.0 (postinstall executed)
build 9873: yarn install -> supply-sdk@3.3.0
```
alex.kim: i'm reverting payments-integration to tag v2026-03-19-last-green and will trigger a manual build + scan. pausing all merges for the repo.
vendor_status_bot: vendor advisory posted: supply-sdk maintainer account was compromised; malicious packages were published and subsequently rolled back. compromised versions: 3.2.5, 3.3.0. IOCs (sha256): abcdef1234567890..., 12345fedcba67890... public notice: https://supply-sdk.io/security/notice-2026-03-19
devsec_irma: uploading IOCs to our internal denylist and kicking off `npm audit` / Snyk scans. also scanning container images for any persisted artifacts or dropped files.
maria_ciso: escalate to SOC + legal. @legal_ash please evaluate regulatory/comms impact. hold on external customer comms until we scope impact.
legal_ash: acknowledged. i'll need the list of affected services and whether any secrets or customer data could have been exfiltrated during those builds. cc: ops-cs if customer-facing work required.
samir: inventory so far: payments, ingestion-batch, analytics-worker. quick check of build logs: secrets used are ephemeral env vars decrypted from KMS; no DB creds were in plaintext. i'm pulling KMS decrypt logs now.
devsec_irma: if KMS decrypts >0 outside normal windows, we should rotate keys and rewrap secrets immediately. proposed steps: 1) create new key version 2) re-encrypt secrets with new key 3) update CI to use new key versions 4) revoke old key usage for build service accounts. i can script steps for aws kms / google kms. example (AWS):
```
# create new key
aws kms create-key --description "incident rotate build secrets 2026-03-19"
# rewrap secrets (example)
aws kms encrypt --key-id <new-key-id> --plaintext "$(aws ssm get-parameter --name /ci/secret --with-decryption --query Parameter.Value --output text)" --output text
```
laura.platform: RBAC change: removed 'deploy' permission from service-account `ci-runner@redwood` in staging+prod. will restore via canary once builds validated.
sec_ops_bot: added audit log filters for packageInstall events + kms:Decrypt events for affected projects; logs forwarded to #incidents and SOC.
alex.kim: do we need to notify customers now or wait for further evidence of exploitation? any signs of outbound C2 from build agents?
maria_ciso: hold external comms until we confirm exploitation. internal notice to stakeholders within 4 hours. if we find evidence of PII or keys exfiltrated, follow incident comms playbook and notify affected customers ASAP.
vendor_status_bot: vendor follow-up: they've revoked the publisher token, rotated maintainers' auth, and provided a safe rebuild (3.2.6) signed with key 0x1234abc. they advise verifying package signatures and hashes before restoring.
devsec_irma: action items i'm owning: block registry egress, add package denylist, rotate build secrets & rewrap KMS. samir — please own RBAC revert/validation and full repo scan. maria — comms & escalation.
samir: kicking off `snyk test --all-projects` and `trivy fs /path/to/checkout` across affected repos; will post results and any suspicious file paths.
laura.platform: firewall rule applied, dependabot auto-updates paused, CI pipelines switched to manual for critical repos only.
sec_ops_bot: update: vendor says this was a publisher token compromise (not npm registry breach). monitoring for other packages from the same publisher namespace.
maria_ciso: scheduling post-incident review for tomorrow 11:00. incident id INC-2026-0319-07. please add any timeline notes to the incident doc.
legal_ash: preparing draft internal notice and checklist for regulator notification if necessary. tagging ops-cs for customer coordination.
alex.kim: thanks all — payments remains on hold until we have a clean build and verified package signatures. :thumbsup:
